Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/yanking, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or causing disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling powerless, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Sigi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sigi.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the people's representative institution of Sigi Regency Region as an element of the Regional government administrator.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Sigi Regency.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
8. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
9. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
10. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threat of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death.
12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of distrust or severe psychological suffering in a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence. 15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of violations of Human Rights (HAM), or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to the family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is temporary housing, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 25

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Sigi Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation.

e. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

a. actively participating in programs and activities initiated by the Government, Regional Government, or other parties as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation;
b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation.

Article 8

The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, include prevention, handling and recovery actions for women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 25

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter b

Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Based on the provisions in Article 41 of Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage ("Marriage Law"), it is stated that the consequences of the dissolution of a marriage due to divorce are:

a. Both the mother or father remain obliged to care for and educate their children, solely based on the interests of the child, if there is a dispute regarding custody of the children, the Court gives its decision.
b. The father who is responsible for all maintenance and education costs required by the child, if the father in reality cannot fulfill such obligation, the court may determine that the mother share such costs.
c. The Court may require the former husband to provide living expenses and/or determine an obligation for the former wife.

The only rule that clearly and explicitly provides guidance for judges in deciding the granting of custody rights over the child is contained in Article 105 of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) which states: "In the event of divorce:

a) custody of a child who has not yet reached mumayyiz or is not yet 12 years old is the mother's right.
b) custody of a child who has reached mumayyiz is handed over to the child to choose between the father or mother as the holder of custody rights.
c) custody costs are borne by the father."

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter a

What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/yanking, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or causing disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling powerless, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

Article 9

(1) In administering protection for women and children victims of violence, the community may:

a. form family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

17. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
18. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to the family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/office/body/bureau within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
25. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
26. Safe House is temporary housing, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

What is meant by the principle of humanity is an existential state of humans as living beings with reason who are attached to natural rights that are innate and must be acknowledged, appreciated, and respected by everyone, including specific aspects inherent in women according to their gender, which in the process of implementing protection for women and children victims of acts of violence must be respected and fulfilled by the state, including among others women's and children's human rights, protection and security as victims of acts of violence, obtaining the best service, inexpensive and fast, sensitivity and empathy, and maintaining their confidentiality as victims of acts of violence.

Letter b

What is meant by the principle of justice, is a mental state of every human being who inherently/naturally wants to obtain a sense of justice as part of society and/or a sense of justice is fulfilled for everyone in their position as citizens. In relation to the protection of women and children victims of acts of violence whose implementation is regulated through this regional regulation, it must fulfill the principle of justice at least including gender equality, legal certainty, presumption of innocence, equality of rights before the law, not blaming the victim, the best interests of the victim. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation.

(2) Financing assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of Regional finance.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Letter a

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling powerless, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

b. activities initiated by the community as long as they do not conflict with the principles of protection for women and children established in this Regional Regulation.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling powerless, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling powerless, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or demeaning of self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act that violates the human dignity of a person based on gender discrimination that targets the body and sexuality of a person, which results in or may result in physical, psychological, economic, sexual, political and/or social harm or suffering to the victim. This formulation is the essence of the findings of 15 forms of sexual violence, among others: 1) Rape; An attack in the form of forced sexual intercourse using the penis towards the vagina, anus or mouth of the victim. It can also use fingers or other objects. The attack is carried out with violence, threats of violence, detention, psychological pressure, abuse of power, or by taking advantage of a coercive environment. Indecent assault is another term for rape known in the Indonesian legal system. This term is used when rape is committed outside of forced penetration of the penis into the vagina and when sexual intercourse occurs with a person who is not yet able to give full consent, for example to a child or someone under 18 years of age.

Sexual violence also includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or child or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of restricting and/or prohibiting family members from working properly.

Letter e

What is meant by "restriction of movement" is restricting the movement of the wife or child in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting them from gathering and socializing in society and restricting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or relating with their families.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence against women and children that occur within the household as well as outside the household will destroy the lives of families, communities, governance, nation, and state. Therefore, the Regional Government of Sigi Regency is obligated to provide protection for women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, Law

Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

The Protection of Women and Children victims of violence is also an obligation as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Government of Sigi Regency has made various efforts to provide Protection to Women and Children Victims of Violence, however this is still far from expectations, due to the absence of sustainable work synergy from the concerned parties, including the still very minimal understanding of the community caused by various things, including the still strong patriarchal culture and entrenched poverty, handling by parties that have not been well coordinated. Therefore, the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence was created to provide legal certainty and protection for victims.

The Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from efforts to prevent various forms of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government and Provincial Government, other Regional/city Governments, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Academics, Journalists and other stakeholders who are concerned and agree with the ideals of realizing a peaceful world without violence against women and children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 16

(1) In order to maximize protection services for women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government through P2TP2A establishes an institutional system and work procedures that ensure integration, cooperation and sustainability in its programs and activities involving relevant parties in the Region.

(2) Further provisions regarding the organization and work procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.
